question.text: What is FIMMDA's primary role in the interest rate derivatives ecosystem?

answer.text: It is a voluntary market body/industry association for the bond, money and derivatives markets, engaged in market development, regulator interface, market practices, benchmarks/new products, and specified IRD conventions
It is the primary regulator of the G-Sec market
It operates the NDS-OM trading platform
It clears and settles all G-Sec transactions

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook describes FIMMDA (Fixed Income Money Market and Derivatives Association of India) as a voluntary market body/industry association for the bond, money and derivatives markets. Its activities cover market development, interfacing with the regulator, market practices, benchmarks/new products, and specified IRD conventions. The Trap: Option B overstates FIMMDA's role — it is not the primary regulator of the G-Sec market. NDS-OM is operated by an exchange/CCIL-side platform, not FIMMDA. Clearing and settlement of G-Sec transactions is handled by the clearing infrastructure, not FIMMDA. Note: Source-backed to NISM-Series-IV workbook (Dec 2025), pages 286-288 (FIMMDA role and functions), with cross-references on pages 113 and 239 noting that FBIL is responsible for G-Sec and SDL valuation in current arrangements.
